correctness.rationale: In diameter two, every color at least two is unique because its separation requirement is at least two, while color one is independent. A block containing a higher-colored vertex dominates the whole graph. Two disjoint color-one-only blocks cannot both dominate because color-one vertices are pairwise nonadjacent, so at most one such block is possible, and it is dominating exactly when the entire color-one class is maximal independent. This yields the lower bound on the largest color, the equality criterion at larger k, and the k+1 construction. Exhaustive direct checking on every labeled diameter-two graph through order five agrees with the formula.

originality.rationale: The initiating paper proves only the optimal-color threshold for diameter-two graphs, namely the largest number of broadcast-dominating blocks supported by an optimal packing coloring. The new statement determines the entire \(\chi_{S,k}\) profile for all \(k\) and identifies its tail exactly with the cardinality spectrum of maximal independent sets. Targeted published-finding corpus and web searches found no equivalent tail formula or complete-multipartite specialization.
residual_risks: The invariant is only days old, so concurrent follow-up work may not yet be indexed.

value.rationale: The result is a natural complete classification for the newly introduced invariant on all diameter-two graphs, not a parameter tweak on a single small family. It determines every \(k\), shows that the entire tail takes only the sharp values \(k\) or \(k+1\), and proves that the profile encodes the cardinality spectrum of maximal independent sets. The complete-multipartite corollary turns this into an explicit part-size formula and exhibits genuine information beyond the prior single threshold.
